text:
A thread 🧵 

First-half analysis: 

England started with confidence
England came into this game knowing that Spain's possession-based football would test their defensive organisation.
However, Thomas Tuchel's side did not simply sit back and allow Spain to dictate proceedings.
England pressed aggressively, competed in midfield and looked dangerous whenever they moved forward.
Jude Bellingham offered quality between the lines.
Declan Rice provided midfield protection and physicality.
Anthony Gordon stretched Spain's defensive line.
Morgan Rogers offered energy and direct attacking movement.
Harry Kane remained a constant threat.
England eventually got their breakthrough when Pau Cubarsí fouled Kane in the penalty area. The England captain converted from the spot in the 45th minute.

Half-time: Spain 0–1 England.

Second-half analysis: 

England punished Spain..
This was where England showed their attacking quality.
In the 53rd minute, Ezri Konsa headed home from a Declan Rice corner to make it 2–0.
Just four minutes later, Ben White finished brilliantly after receiving a pass from Jude Bellingham.
At 3–0, England looked completely in control.
They were clinical, aggressive and took advantage of Spain's defensive vulnerabilities.

The turning point: 

Elliot Anderson's red card♦️
The 63rd-minute dismissal of Elliot Anderson completely changed the complexion of the match.
England were reduced to ten men after Anderson brought down an opponent in the penalty area.
Mikel Oyarzabal converted the resulting penalty in the 65th minute.
Spain immediately gained momentum, and Nico Williams made it 3–2 in the 75th minute.
The final stages became a serious test of England's defensive discipline.
James Trafford produced an outstanding late double save, while Ben White made a crucial intervention to deny Lamine Yamal.
England held on.

Tactical verdict: Tuchel deserves credit
There are three major positives from this performance:
1. England's pressing
They did not allow Spain to enjoy complete comfort in possession. England were proactive rather than simply reactive.
2. Attacking efficiency
Three goals against Spain in Madrid is a significant achievement. England converted their opportunities and punished defensive mistakes.
3. Mental strength
Going down to ten men against a technically gifted Spanish side and protecting a one-goal advantage requires serious concentration and organisation.
The biggest concern, however, is how quickly England lost control after Anderson's dismissal. Their defensive structure became vulnerable, and Spain nearly completed the comeback.

🎙️🇪🇸 LUIS DE LA FUENTE ON PEDRI'S REPEATED BENCHING, ELLIOT ANDERSON'S PERFORMANCE AND ENGLAND'S DOMINANCE!

Q: Why do you keep leaving Pedri on the bench despite his quality and importance to Barcelona?

Luis de la Fuente:

"Pedri is an exceptional footballer. Nobody questions his technical ability, intelligence or importance to Spanish football. But playing for Spain is not just about individual reputation. Every selection is based on what I believe the team needs for a particular opponent.

Against England, I wanted a midfield with physical strength, defensive balance and the ability to make forward runs. That is why I selected Martín Zubimendi, Fabián Ruiz and Mikel Merino.

I understand why people are asking questions. Pedri is a player who can control the rhythm of a match, create opportunities and make difficult situations look simple. But being on the bench does not mean he has lost my confidence. He remains an important player for Spain.

Q: What is your assessment of Elliot Anderson?

Anderson has shown why England trust him in important matches. His energy, aggression and ability to compete in midfield have been noticeable. Alongside Declan Rice, he has helped England disrupt Spain's rhythm.

However, his red card following the challenge on Lamine Yamal was a costly moment. At this level, players must understand when to challenge and when to stay composed. His performance will naturally attract attention, but discipline is just as important as ability.

Q: What about Jude Bellingham and Harry Kane?

Bellingham has brought intensity and personality to England's midfield. His involvement in the attacking moves and ability to arrive in dangerous positions make him extremely difficult to control.

Harry Kane has once again demonstrated his experience. He took responsibility from the penalty spot and gave England the breakthrough just before half-time. That is what you expect from a world-class striker.

Declan Rice has also been influential, providing protection and helping England compete physically in midfield. Ben White and Ezri Konsa deserve credit for their contributions at the back.

Q: Spain have Lamine Yamal, Fabián Ruiz and Martín Zubimendi. What went wrong?

Lamine Yamal has continued to show his quality. He has been one of Spain's biggest attacking threats, and winning the penalty after Anderson's challenge was an important moment.

Fabián Ruiz and Zubimendi have tried to provide control, while Mikel Merino offers a different attacking dimension. But we need more consistency across the team.

Pau Cubarsí will also have to learn from the penalty incident involving Harry Kane. These small mistakes can change the direction of a major match.

The players must take responsibility, improve their decisions and understand that possession alone does not win football matches.

Q: Will Pedri return to the starting XI?

Pedri knows what I expect from him. He has the quality to influence matches, and there will be opportunities for him. My responsibility is to select the team that gives Spain the best balance.

I do not select players because of their club reputation or public popularity. I select them because of what the team needs."

🔥 THE BIG QUESTION: Is Luis de la Fuente right to keep Pedri on the bench, or should Spain build their midfield around the Barcelona star?

My take is that Elon Musk should keep his options open, but he shouldn’t rush into moving Tesla’s operations because of a political disagreement.

Florida may offer a business-friendly environment, but relocating a major factory is a massive decision involving workers, infrastructure, suppliers, costs and long-term investment.

At the same time, Governor Gina Hinojosa should understand that states compete for businesses, jobs and investment. If Texas creates an environment that makes companies feel unwelcome, other states will be ready to benefit.

Ultimately, this should be about economic growth, not political ego. Elon should choose the state that offers Tesla the strongest long-term future, while both governors should focus on creating jobs and attracting investment rather than trading political shots.

text:
Tim McGraw was 11 when he learned that baseball star Tug McGraw was his biological father. Tug refused to acknowledge him for years, then offered college support on the condition that Tim stop contacting him and his family.

Tim grew up in Louisiana using his stepfather's surname. While searching his mother's closet, he found a birth certificate naming Tug as his father, a player whose baseball card already hung on Tim's wall.

His mother arranged a meeting in Houston. Tug was friendly but told the boy to think of him as a friend, not a father. Tim continued writing afterward, but the messages went unanswered.

Near the end of high school, Tim needed help with college. He says Tug's representatives offered financial support through an agreement requiring Tim to end all contact. Tim agreed to consider it only if they met one last time.

At dinner in Houston, Tim told Tug he would sign the agreement and disappear from his life, but first asked: "Do you think you're my dad?" Tug answered, "Yes, I believe I am," and dropped the agreement.

Recognition did not instantly create a close relationship. Tim says another year passed before they began spending time together. He later visited Tug in Philadelphia and formed relationships with his half-siblings.

When Tug developed brain cancer in 2003, Tim helped arrange treatment and supported him through his final months. Tug died at Tim's cabin outside Nashville on January 5, 2004, with Tim and other relatives beside him.

Tim later said he waited beside his dying father for an apology that never came. In his 2026 Tim Ferriss interview, he said he never hated Tug, despite the years his father refused to claim him.
